record.summary: Decision of the NPC Standing Committee making 14 changes to the Cybersecurity Law. It adds an article on AI, Article 20 of the amended law: the state supports basic AI theory research and R&D of key technologies such as algorithms, builds training-data resources, computing power and other infrastructure, improves AI ethics norms, strengthens risk monitoring, assessment and safety supervision, and promotes AI applications and healthy development; it also supports using AI and other new technologies to improve cybersecurity protection. Other changes raise the penalties for network operators and critical information infrastructure operators.
record.notes: Adopted on 28 Oct 2025 at the 18th session of the 14th NPC Standing Committee and in force from 1 Jan 2026. The Cybersecurity Law is republished with the changes and its articles renumbered. Besides the AI article, the Decision adds an article on Party leadership of cybersecurity work and the overall national security concept (new Art. 3), requires network operators handling personal information to comply with the Civil Code and the Personal Information Protection Law, raises fines up to 10 million yuan for especially serious consequences, adds penalties for selling uncertified critical network equipment and dedicated security products, and allows lighter or no penalties in the cases the Administrative Penalty Law provides.

english_version.by: Etcetera Language Group, Inc., for the Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), Georgetown University

record.scope_note: Not AI-specific: an amendment to the Cybersecurity Law, included for the article on AI research, ethics norms, risk monitoring and assessment and safety supervision that it adds (Art. 20 of the amended law).

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored and read: the Decision on the NPC website (npc.gov.cn, copy of 11 Oct 2026, unchanged when the archiver checked it on 18 Oct 2026), which gives the title, the adoption on 28 Oct 2025 at the 18th session of the 14th NPC Standing Committee, its 14 changes including the new AI article (Art. 20), and the entry into force on 1 Jan 2026; and the CAC's republication of the Xinhua text of 28 Oct 2025 (cac.gov.cn, copy of 11 Oct 2026), with the same text. No stored file gives the number of the presidential order that promulgated the Decision, so official_identifier stays empty. Version 1's note that China has not adopted a comprehensive AI law rests on no stored file and was removed, as was its sentence on what the summary covers. The English title is a rendering; no English text by a Chinese public body was found. CSET's English translation of the Cybersecurity Law as amended in October 2025 (cset.georgetown.edu, stored in this run on 18 Oct 2026; translator Etcetera Language Group, translation date 14 Apr 2026, from the NPC text) is recorded as english_version: it translates the amended law, not the Decision itself, and confirms that the AI provision is Article 20 of the amended law and that the amended law took effect on 1 Jan 2026.

summary.quote: 三、增加一条，作为第二十条：“国家支持人工智能基础理论研究和算法等关键技术研发，推进训练数据资源、算力等基础设施建设，完善人工智能伦理规范，加强风险监测评估和安全监管，促进人工智能应用和健康发展。

summary.locator: page 6, Article 20 of the amended law (translation)
summary.quote: Article 20 The state supports basic theoretical research in artificial intelligence (AI) and the research and development of key technologies such as algorithms

notes.quote: 一、增加一条，作为第三条：“网络安全工作坚持中国共产党的领导，贯彻总体国家安全观，统筹发展和安全，推进网络强国建设。”
“网络运营者处理个人信息，应当遵守本法和《中华人民共和国民法典》、《中华人民共和国个人信息保护法》等法律、行政法规的规定。”
